summary: Phase 5 — UTM Campaign Links builder verified end-to-end. Backend: 10/10 pytest in test_utm_links.py PASS. POST /api/admin/utm-links returns the full doc {id (utm_xxx), name, base_url, params:{utm_source,utm_medium,utm_campaign,utm_content,utm_term}, url, created_at}; slugs are lowercased & non-alphanumeric-hyphenated (e.g. 'LinkedIn'→'linkedin', 'Beta Dec'→'beta-dec'); existing querystring on base_url is preserved (foo=bar & x=1 kept, utm_* added). Empty source returns 422 (Pydantic strip check → 400 in code path OK per contract). GET /api/admin/utm-links returns {days:30, rows:[…]} newest-first with per-row stats {sessions, signups, demo_clicks, conversion_pct}. DELETE /api/admin/utm-links/{id} returns {deleted:1} and the row disappears from the list; analytics_events untouched. Auth: non-admin (no cookie) is rejected on GET/POST/DELETE (401). Stats aggregation end-to-end: created a linkedin/post/<slug> link, fired page_view + waitlist_success + book_demo_click via /api/analytics/track with matching properties.source/medium/campaign — the row's stats.sessions>=1, signups>=1, demo_clicks>=1, conversion_pct>0. Regression: full non-generation suite 56/56 PASS (test_utm_links + test_phase1 + test_phase1_ab_digest + test_phase1_demo). Frontend Playwright: /admin?tab=utm renders data-testid=utm-section; sidebar side-utm href is /admin?tab=utm and clicking it navigates & renders utm-section; tab-utm click also navigates. All 7 preset chips render with data-testid utm-preset-linkedin_post/linkedin_article/linkedin_dm/linkedin_ad/email_outbound/community_post/custom; clicking linkedin_ad fills source=linkedin & medium=cpc; clicking linkedin_post fills source=linkedin & medium=post. Form fields utm-name/utm-campaign/utm-source/utm-medium/utm-content/utm-term all present. utm-preview updates live and produces kebab-case params (verified: utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=e2e_ui_1784730013). utm-save posts to /api/admin/utm-links using window.location.origin as base_url; success toast 'Campaign link created' displayed; new row appears in table with data-testid=utm-row-{id}. Each row has utm-copy-{id}, utm-open-{id}, utm-delete-{id}. Copy writes r.url to clipboard (verified via navigator.clipboard.readText after granting clipboard-write). Delete confirms via window.confirm and removes the row on accept. Table columns render sessions / demo_clicks / signups / conversion_pct% from row.stats. Attribution end-to-end: after localStorage.clear() + visit /?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=beta_dec, localStorage.avs_attribution = {source:'linkedin', medium:'post', campaign:'beta_dec', referrer_host:null} — so subsequent track() calls will carry these in properties.source/medium/campaign and roll up into the matching UTM row stats.

minor.issue: Empty string source ('') returns 422 (Pydantic HTTPException wrapper) rather than 400. Contract spec asked for 400. Consider validating in the route body BEFORE Pydantic strip so `raise HTTPException(400, 'source is required')` actually fires — currently the .strip() check runs but Pydantic still emits 422 for other missing/blank scenarios.

No duplicate-detection: creating two links with the same source/medium/campaign yields two rows whose stats aggregation query is identical, so the same events count into both rows. Consider a UNIQUE index on (utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign) or dedup by params hash.

ui_bugs.issue: navigator.clipboard.writeText() is not wrapped in try/catch — in contexts without clipboard-write permission (older browsers, insecure iframes) it throws an unhandled promise rejection that surfaces as the CRA runtime-error overlay. First playwright run without permissions showed 'Uncaught runtime errors: Failed to execute writeText on Clipboard: Write permission denied.'

action_items: MINOR: Wrap navigator.clipboard.writeText in UtmLinksTab.copy() with try/catch (or .catch()) and toast.error('Copy failed — check browser permissions') on rejection to avoid CRA error overlay in restricted browser contexts.

OPTIONAL: Return 400 (not 422) when source is empty by validating the payload before Pydantic parsing, e.g. accept `source: str = Field(min_length=1)` OR keep the current post-parse check but add an explicit BadRequest handler.
OPTIONAL: Add dedup on (utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign) to prevent two identical-slug rows double-counting the same analytics events.
OPTIONAL (pre-existing from prior passes, unchanged): /api/analytics/track & /api/experiments/{exp}/{cid} still unauthenticated + no rate-limit.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py _link_stats matches on properties.source only if utm_source is present, but analytics events also carry properties.variant/etc. — the query is correct today, but if utm_medium is None in the doc, the match doc omits properties.medium (`if p.get("utm_medium")`), which means a link created with source=linkedin only will match ANY medium event for linkedin — could be surprising if users create both a 'source-only' link and a 'source+medium' link.

UtmLinksTab.jsx uses window.confirm() for delete — inconsistent with the rest of the admin panel which uses shadcn Dialog components (see AdminPanel.jsx). Migrate to AlertDialog for a11y & style consistency.

UtmLinksTab.jsx computes previewUrl on every keystroke via URLSearchParams — fine, but the `kebab()` regex differs slightly from backend `_clean_slug` (frontend keeps underscores, backend also keeps underscores, so consistent — good). Note however: frontend regex `/[^a-z0-9_-]+/g` matches empty string as 0 replacements — OK, but leading/trailing hyphens are stripped only via `.replace(/^-|-$/g,'')` which only strips ONE — for e.g. '--foo--' it becomes '-foo-'. Prefer `.replace(/^-+|-+$/g,'')`.

server.py _clean_slug returns None for empty input which is correct, but in _compose_url the `if v` check skips None values. Combined this means an empty utm_content is silently dropped — good — but the returned `params` dict still contains utm_content:None, which leaks null values into the JSON response. Consider filtering None out of params too for a cleaner API surface.

server.py utm_create does base = payload.base_url or (str(request.base_url)…replace(':8001', '')). Fragile string replacement — if the reverse-proxy ever runs on a different internal port this breaks. Use urlparse + _replace(netloc=…) instead.
